title: Turrican II: The Final Fight
build: Triangle disk release from the C64Games archive

records.c: Actor type three permits only one linked group, reserves three extra slots and initializes four body components from $AE1E-$AE31. The shared health counter starts at two. The controller checks a four-row character-damage span and wheel contact; death awards 2000 points and converts all four parts into freshly initialized type-seven actors with per-part X steps and timer-selected phases. Movement reverses at terrain and uses the twenty-step vertical curve at $AEC8 after an overhead obstacle.

Scan the other actor slots for type three; a prior linked group releases this newly initialized source slot. Otherwise preserve its origin and try reserving three free component slots.

Build the screen pointer and scan two columns across four rows for a damaging character. Erase a detected hit, subtract its damage-table amount from shared health, and flash all four component colours zero on survival. The shared kill flag also destroys the group.

Use terrain samples to reverse horizontal direction or start a vertical-curve index of nineteen. Add signed X/Y increments to the group origin, copy the four component offsets and release all linked slots on bounds failure.
Clear all four component types and X coordinates, and restore each component's default Y before continuing the actor scan.

Actor type four initializes two side-by-side sprites and remembers the controlling slot. The active controller keeps the timer prescaler at fifty, permits standing on its platform and checks a centred, grounded player's downward joystick input. Acceptance installs the lift raster sequence, hides the normal lower sprites and selects a facing-dependent three-sprite player pose.

Switch to the playfield video settings and update player/platform sprite X positions. Increment the camera row. At row $A0 stop the lift, restore the normal raster chain and install $7292 as the player hook. Otherwise toggle screen selection and jump through $98EA/$98EC to the appropriate one-row screen copy.

Decode forty character columns from the current map phase using the shared nibble-exchanged block format. Patch source/destination operands, draw the new row, fill its colour buffer and advance both vertical map-phase pointers with the level's 170-byte row stride.

Stabilize the panel split, select panel video settings, copy twenty colour rows upward and append the forty generated edge colours. Re-enter the lift playfield handler; $727B restores the normal playfield display register at its scheduled split.
Use the retained raster delay table to align the display-register update, restore $D011 and return through the common interrupt exit.

On its first flagged call, remove the lift actors, start two type-five attached effects and patch five generated-code opcodes from $9A49. When the first attached effect's counter reaches zero, clear those opcodes, restore the normal player hook and clear special-weapon/exit flags.

Actor type five uses its subtype to select an X offset beside the player, shape $FE and a countdown at $998F. Each update decrements that countdown and follows a sixteen-step signed X/Y curve; expiry releases the actor.

Actor type six uses state zero as a hidden regional controller, delaying forty updates and then running for fifty. It allocates upward-moving hazards at timer-selected X positions when the sampled bottom terrain is passable. On selected camera rows it can instead create a two-part falling emitter. Its controller also subtracts three pixels from player Y while the player movement flag is active.

State one cycles three shapes and moves upward by its saved speed until it leaves the playfield. Other nonzero states descend one pixel per update; the lower sprite of the paired falling emitter can spawn type-sixteen projectiles with signed motion from $9AE3/$9AEB. Leaving the bottom clears the pair-active flag.

Actor type seven accepts player and character contact. On a detected hit in state zero it creates up to two state-one children, then explodes. Children and parents award subtype-selected score amounts. Terrain reverses horizontal direction and selects rising/falling positions in the curve at $AD74. State zero cycles four frames; child state one retains its shape.

Search free actor slots and create up to two type-seven state-one children. Give each shape $A2, colour one, timer-selected horizontal speed and vertical phase, and a source-relative position. Continue into the parent explosion path even if no child slot remains.

Check horizontal bounds, reverse X direction on side terrain and choose vertical curve indices at the floor/ceiling. Add the saved signed X step and decreasing-index curve Y step, then animate the original state-zero actor.

Actor type eight starts state zero with fifteen health, a timer-selected wait and shape $A5. It plays a six-step animation and allocates a type-eight state-one child at the chosen frame. Children begin with two health, fall toward the player's height or solid terrain, wait ten updates and then move horizontally toward the selected side. Damage and contact award state-selected scores.
Advance the six-step shape/duration sequence. At frame three, allocate a child with two health, facing chosen from player X and a source-relative position. Completion restarts a thirty-update wait.

Select the child's facing shape. State one falls four pixels until it reaches terrain or the player's vertical span; state two waits ten updates then moves horizontally by a signed step. Terrain starts its explosion, while bounds release it.

Actor type nine uses its subtype to select a fixed shape, Y offset and collision size. Subtype zero is a nondamageable vertical projectile path. Other subtypes have ten health and emit type-nine state-zero shots every twenty-three updates, with signed Y step selected by subtype. Destroying the emitter awards 250 points; its shots release on solid terrain or vertical bounds.

Reload the emission counter with twenty-two, allocate a type-nine state-zero shot and give it shape $BF, colour one and the subtype-selected signed Y velocity. The actor continuation later removes it at terrain or bounds.
Rebuild its terrain pointer, choose upper or lower sample from the velocity sign and test passability. Move by the saved signed Y step only while the sample and vertical bounds permit.

Actor type ten starts with ten reward steps, permits standing and underside bumping, and changes to shape $9D on its first character hit. Subsequent hits count down a five-hit divider and create timer-selected rewards; exhaustion explodes it for 5000 points. Launched rewards use the separate thirty-one-entry curve at $9D8A and become ordinary pickups on landing.
Combine standing and underside flags across eleven platform slots. Apply the nine-entry bump curve, snap a standing player's Y to the top and make a new underside bump advance the reward counter.

Reflect signed X motion at side terrain, advance the vertical curve and convert to freshly initialized type-two pickup on landing or final phase. The side selector reads the unindexed $BC6C while the step itself reads $BC6C,X.

Actor type eleven starts at fixed X/Y with a timer-selected delay, shape, horizontal step and curve length. After the delay it requests an explosion sound, subtracts the reward curve's Y increments and adds its saved X step. Curve completion restores the ordinary player hook and releases the actor.

Actor type twelve waits for a grounded player, takes over the player hook at $7C19 and initializes a large multiband scene using the same matrices as the boss. Its next state copies the exit pose arrays, clears counters, installs raster hooks and seeds five columns of X coordinates in the RAM allocation at $F140.

Drive the automatic rightward player motion and separate enlarged foreground sprite. A matching camera position starts a staged sequence: adjust band counts, load departure coordinates, issue timer-spaced effects, then move five columns until the final high-X/position condition jumps to the shared next-level transition.

Select three departure phases from $BCE8. The first installs reduced band limits and initial positions. The second counts timer-based effects and a sound pause. Later updates move five columns by six pixels after independent delays; the final high-X and X threshold enters $098E.
Keep the foreground sprite X fixed at $4B and its horizontal expansion mask set to one during the special raster sequence.

Restore thirty-two source bitmap bytes from map-overlaid storage at $9082 into the two animated glyphs, reset four palette cells and set the special-weapon flags and first raster line. Fall through to the per-update callback.

Patch and call the camera-phase-selected glyph-scroll helper through $AFE0/$AFE9. Choose terrain animation regions from the two-byte camera X and Y. In one region, allocate a type-six controller if absent; remove its state-zero controller on leaving that region.

Rotate a double-height character pattern and two adjacent pairs in opposite directions. Copy two phase-selected glyph frames from $FF40/$FF60. Terrain characters $66-$69 can push player X one half-pixel when neighbouring terrain permits and the opposing joystick direction is not held.
When the special-weapon flag at $081A is clear, rotate two sixteen-byte glyph halves upward by two row bytes, preserving their first two bytes at the end.
Rotate the two sixteen-byte glyph halves downward by two row bytes, preserving the final two bytes at their beginnings.

Actor type fifteen waits for a grounded player and neutral directional input after the camera threshold. It installs special player, camera and raster hooks, then controls five sprite columns with twenty-one stored bands. Six components begin with thirty health apiece. Once they are destroyed, a central target becomes vulnerable with a separate two-byte health counter initially $0100. Final death awards 50000 points and starts the scripted departure sequence.
Operand byte 1 of the LDA instruction at $7FF4, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.

Disable ordinary camera and actor raster callbacks, install boss hooks and patch the screen pointer stores for the active page. Clear transient exchange state and call $8720 to establish the body's vertical band coordinates.

Restore any outstanding bitmap-row exchange, then choose live or dying update paths from the source actor state. During life restore the central colour pattern when selected, run component state, scripted motion, contact, damage and terrain-shot updates, and alternate a selected shape. The pre-render hook chooses visible bands before returning to the actor scan.

Select palette parameters from the body Y position. On action completion read the next of fifty-two action IDs from $AF60, then patch the JSR from split address tables $9F33/$9FDD and load its duration/speed from $A087/$A131. Reset action-local state, run the action and apply its temporary screen-shake phase to $16.

Operand byte 2 of the JSR instruction at $8142, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.

Decrement the action duration. Move the final and first groups of stored column coordinates left by the selected speed, toggling high-X masks on borrow. Copy the terminal positions across the repeated body bands. Completion requests screen shake and sound.

Decrement duration and move the stored column positions right with the selected speed. Toggle high-X masks on carry, repeat the terminal positions across bands and finish with the shared action-completion path. If all first high-X bits are set on completion, rebuild the vertical band coordinates.
Copy each column's terminal X position through its twenty preceding band slots, skipping two designated indices. Replicate the last high-X mask across the stored band mask array.
Count down duration and alternate two Y increments from $A1DB before propagating the body Y coordinates to preceding bands.
Choose a timer-based repetition count, alternate short rightward and leftward movements, and finish each oscillation with screen shake and sound. The selected action duration controls its first leg.
Count down the saved duration and end the active action at zero.
Subtract the selected speed from the last two-byte band Y coordinate, propagate the twenty preceding coordinates at twenty-one-pixel spacing and end when duration expires.
Add the selected speed to the last two-byte band Y coordinate, then propagate preceding bands at twenty-one-pixel spacing. Duration zero ends the action.
Starting at the final band, subtract twenty-one pixels with borrow to fill the preceding twenty low/high Y entries.

Test the player against the selected moving body section. On capture patch the player hook to $83D9, select the final action-sequence positions and install the captured pose. The action then moves the selected column entries outward, pauses with colour toggling and retracts them unless capture or duration ends it.

Derive player X/Y from the selected body section and its high-X mask. Alternate the captured player's shape on a three-update divider. When the horizontal position exits the active range, restore the normal player hook and put the player at the lower Y coordinate.
After the death counter becomes negative, add the indexed death curve to body Y, propagate the bands and perform the normal rightward movement leg. Continue into player contact handling.
Convert the first body X to half-pixels and save it. If its adjusted left boundary reaches the player, enter the shared damage hook; otherwise return.

Find the first eligible body band and sample three pairs of terrain characters across five successive rows using three offset arrays. A damaging character is erased, then matched against the six active component bands or the enabled central band. Component hits subtract through the shared damage table and start flashing or explosion states. Central hits use the two-byte health counter and initiate final death on high-byte underflow.

Subtract the terrain damage-table value from the selected component's byte counter. Surviving hits flash its selected colour cells; underflow selects explosion state two, starts the thirteen-step animation and awards 1500 points.

Accept a central hit only at band ten, subtract damage from the two-byte counter at $A87F/$A880 and flash all five columns on survival. Final underflow starts the forty-four-update death counter, increments the actor state and disables the player update hook.

Flash all five colour columns while the counter runs; after it becomes negative hide selected central shape cells. Once body Y reaches the terminal high-byte state, restore ordinary camera/raster hooks, request eleven type-eleven exit fragments, reset palette parameters and award 50000 points.

Cycle six component slots and create a left-moving two-character terrain shot when a component is active and visible. Five independent shot slots save their underlying characters and colours, restore them on movement, and draw $B2/$B3 in colour nine. Solid terrain or the left edge removes the shot.

Set the final body Y to $0158 and fill twenty-one two-byte band coordinates at twenty-one-pixel spacing. Copy selected column X coordinates into repeated indices and derive two high-X masks from the selected body column.
Convert wheel form if necessary, cycle the normal seven-frame walking animation and move the player right until half-pixel X reaches $4A.
Install the scripted movement/weapon flags, set the exit flag, clear wheel form and set the saved weapon parameter to $FF.

Cycle six component states, update their selected live colour cells and animate destroyed components with the thirteen-step source arrays at $9044/$90EE/$9198. When all six component states are zero, change the three damage-offset entries and central shape, then enable the central target.

Search the stored two-byte body Y coordinates for a visible band. Save current/previous band indices, prepare five hardware sprite Y coordinates and the surface scanline, and perform the bitmap-row exchange at selected character subphases.

Copy five shape pointers into both screens, set five sprite X coordinates and colours and merge their high-X masks. For an above-screen band, wait until the following band is near before installing its Y coordinates.

Reuse hardware sprites three through seven for successive stored bands. Read five shape, X and colour columns, restore prior exchanged bitmap bytes and select the next visible band. Schedule the common lower split when the body or raster bound is reached; at selected subphases exchange the bitmap rows before returning from the interrupt.
